newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.1 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.1 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.1 percent to close at 1.0306 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.0305 to 1.0355 per dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0305 real and selling at 1.0355 reais in a morning auction.
The previous mini-band, set on Nov 11, was between 1.0295 and 1.0345 reais to the dollar.
In the afternoon the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0305 reais per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market.

Dealers said preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Wednesday surplus of around $30 million in late afternoon. But they estimated the market has been holding at least $200 million since the last buy auction by the Central Bank on Nov 11.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.1 percent to end at 1.0355 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.098 per greenback, down 0.46 percent due to a reduction in the supply of dollars, traders said.
